prompt: Which of the following best distinguishes software engineering from programming?
choices: Software engineering uses more advanced programming languages
Software engineering is programming considered across time, scale, and multiple people, not just whether the code runs once
Software engineering never involves writing code
Software engineering only applies to large companies

prompt: Which sequence puts the SDLC phases in their typical order?
choices: Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance
Design, Requirements, Implementation, Deployment, Testing, Maintenance
Implementation, Requirements, Design, Testing, Maintenance, Deployment
Requirements, Implementation, Design, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance

prompt: Six months after shipping a feature, you open the code to fix a bug and can't figure out why a particular check exists. Which practice from this lesson would most directly have prevented this problem?
choices: Writing the code faster the first time
Leaving context behind, such as a commit message or comment explaining the reasoning, not just the change itself
Using a more advanced programming language
Skipping design discussion to ship sooner

prompt: You've just cloned an unfamiliar small open-source repository and want to get oriented efficiently. What does this lesson recommend as the first step?
choices: Read every file in the repo top to bottom, in alphabetical order
Read the README to learn the project's purpose and see a usage example before opening any code
Immediately run the test suite and skip the README entirely
Search GitHub issues for open bugs first

prompt: In the Requests library walkthrough, what did opening requests/api.py reveal?
choices: That the library has no public API
That functions like get() and post() are thin wrappers that all funnel into a shared request()/Session code path
That all HTTP logic is separately duplicated inside each verb function
That the library's tests are defined inside api.py

prompt: Why does a commit message like "reject expired reset tokens; previously any token, even stale ones, still worked (#412)" matter more in team software engineering than in a one-off solo script?
choices: It makes the code execute faster
It communicates intent and context to teammates and future maintainers who weren't present when the change was made
It is a syntax requirement of most programming languages
It removes the need to write any tests

prompt: A team ships a feature, and three weeks later a user reports it breaks when their name contains an apostrophe. The team patches the bug and updates the input-validation tests. Which SDLC phase does this activity mainly represent?
choices: Requirements
Design
Maintenance
Deployment
